subject.title: Feature: post-process NO_REPLY to suppress partial leaks

question: Should OpenClaw broaden NO_REPLY suppression for generic mixed trailing or contained payloads, and where should the boundary sit between silent-intent text and legitimate substantive replies that mention or append the token?
rationale: Current main deliberately preserves some substantive trailing-token replies while the issue asks for broader suppression to avoid internal text leaks; that is a shared message-delivery and security contract decision rather than mechanical cleanup.

options.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
options.body: Define and reuse a shared classifier that suppresses internal or silent-intent mixed payloads while preserving legitimate substantive replies.

options.title: Use blanket own-line suppression
options.body: Suppress any reply ending with a trailing or own-line NO_REPLY token and accept that some currently visible substantive replies may be dropped.

options.title: Keep the narrow policy
options.body: Document that only token-only, punctuation-only, reasoning-prefixed, and scoped cron cases are suppressed, then retarget broad suppression requests.

recommendation.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
recommendation.body: Define and reuse a shared classifier that suppresses internal or silent-intent mixed payloads while preserving legitimate substantive replies.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans shared reply delivery and product/security policy, and steipete is tied to the central mixed-content auto-reply landing history.
